name: df
description: Reports free and used disk space for mounted filesystems.

flags.description: Show inode usage instead of block usage.
Exclude a filesystem type, e.g. -x tmpfs.

examples.output:
Filesystem      Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda2        98G   41G   52G  44% /
tmpfs           7.8G     0  7.8G   0% /dev/shm
/dev/sdb1       916G  612G  258G  71% /data
examples.explanation: Shows each mounted filesystem with size, usage, and mount point. The Use% column tells you when a disk is filling up.

examples.output:
Filesystem     Type  Size  Used Avail Use% Mounted on
/dev/sda3      ext4  197G   88G   99G  48% /home
examples.explanation: Checks a specific path and reveals its filesystem type.

examples.output:
Filesystem     Inodes  IUsed  IFree IUse% Mounted on
/dev/sda2      6.1M    412K   5.7M    7% /
examples.explanation: Inode usage: a filesystem can be "full" even with free space if all inodes are consumed by millions of small files.

about: df reads usage from the kernel for each mounted filesystem. tmpfs entries are RAM-based; squashfs and overlay entries appear in containers and Live systems. A 100% full root filesystem causes failed writes, broken updates, and log loss — monitor Use% regularly.
useCases: Verify that a new disk was mounted correctly.
mistakes: Panic over a nearly full tmpfs — it is RAM-backed and shrinks automatically.
Ignoring inode usage: deleting large files will not help when inodes are exhausted; millions of tiny files must go.
